newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Santos says only partly halted by strike.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Santos says only partly halted by strike.

text.p: Brazil's key port of Santos said a strike by stevedores had not completely paralysed operations and some vessels were loading, while arrivals and warehouse operations were continuing as usual.
"It has partially stopped operations. We have three vessels operating," said a spokeswoman.
There were 21 vessels docked, 17 at the port authority terminal and four at private terminals. Three vessels were loading tallow, liquid gas and oil. The loading of these goods is automated.

"The area of cargo loading onto vessels has stopped," said the spokeswoman, referring to the export terminal where grains are loaded. "The area of truck arrivals for warehouses is operating normally."
She added that she did not know whether the private terminals were operating but did not think they were.

The stevedores went on strike as of 0700 local/1000 GMT over a ruling which allows company workers from steel mill Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) to operate Cosipa's private terminal at the port.
The strike is scheduled to last 48 hours and could spread to national level on Friday if the dispute is not resolved, the stevedores' union said.
